ei1:ibn-badjdja.narrative_tr: İbn Bâcce (Latince: Avempace), Endülüs İslam felsefesinin kurucu figürlerinden olup Tedbîrü'l-Mütevahhid adlı eseriyle tanınır. Bu eserde ideal filozofun toplum içindeki konumunu ele alarak münferit bireyin entelektüel mükemmelliğe ulaşma yolunu tartışmıştır. Aristoteles felsefesini yeniden yorumlayarak İbn Tufeyl ve İbn Rüşd'e zemin hazırlamıştır. Felsefenin yanı sıra müzik, tıp ve astronomi alanlarında da eserler vermiştir. Fas'ta zehirlenerek öldüğü rivayet edilir.
ei1:ibn-badjdja.narrative_en: Ibn Bajja (Latin: Avempace) was a founding figure of Andalusian Islamic philosophy, known for his Tadbir al-Mutawahhid. In this work, he examined the position of the ideal philosopher in society and discussed the solitary individual's path to intellectual perfection. By reinterpreting Aristotelian philosophy, he paved the way for Ibn Tufayl and Ibn Rushd. Beyond philosophy, he also authored works in music, medicine, and astronomy. He reportedly died of poisoning in Morocco.

ei1:ibn-sabln.narrative_tr: İbn Sab'în, Endülüs kökenli mutasavvıf ve filozof olup vahdet-i vücûd anlayışını radikal biçimde yorumlamasıyla tanınır. Kutsal Roma İmparatoru II. Friedrich'in felsefi sorularına verdiği el-Ecvibetü's-Sıkılliyye (Sicilya Cevapları) adlı eseri, Doğu-Batı entelektüel diyalogunun erken örneklerinden biridir. Mürsiye'den ayrılarak Kuzey Afrika ve Mekke'de yaşamıştır. İbn Arabî ekolünden farklı bir vahdet-i vücûd yorumu geliştirmiştir.
ei1:ibn-sabln.narrative_en: Ibn Sabin was a Sufi and philosopher of Andalusian origin, known for his radical interpretation of the unity of existence. His al-Ajwiba al-Siqilliyya (Sicilian Answers), written in response to the philosophical questions of Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II, is an early example of East-West intellectual dialogue. He left Murcia to live in North Africa and Mecca. He developed a distinct interpretation of wahdat al-wujud different from the school of Ibn Arabi.

ei1:kudatku-bilik.narrative_en: Yusuf Khass Hajib authored Kutadgu Bilig, the first major work of Turkic-Islamic literature. Presented to the Karakhanid ruler Tabghach Bughra Khan in 1069-1070, this masnavi treats concepts of ideal governance, justice, wisdom, and happiness through allegorical dialogues. Written in Karakhanid Turkish, it constitutes one of the oldest literary works in the Turkic language. It has survived in three manuscripts.

ei1:muhammad-ii-ai-hanafiya.narrative_en: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya was the son of Caliph Ali and an important figure in early Islamic theology and political history. He studied jurisprudence and theology under his father. His declaration as Mahdi during Mukhtar al-Thaqafi's revolt represents one of the earliest instances of messianic politics in Islam. Though the Kaysaniyya sect is attributed to him, his direct involvement remains debated. He holds a respected position in the Ahl al-Bayt tradition.

ei1:muhammad-c-abduh.narrative_en: Muhammad Abduh was one of the most influential figures of modern Islamic reformism. After studying at al-Azhar, he questioned the causes of decline in the Islamic world under the influence of Jamal al-Din al-Afghani and advocated a rationalist interpretation of Islam. During his tenure as Grand Mufti of Egypt, he supported educational and legal reforms. Through the Tafsir al-Manar project, he initiated the tradition of modern Quranic interpretation. He argued that the gate of ijtihad remains open and that blind imitation must be abandoned.

Based in Qatar, he established a global sphere of influence through television and internet media.

Hadislerin resmî olarak derlenmesini emreden ilk halife olması, İslam ilim tarihinin dönüm noktalarından biridir. Vergi adaleti, gayrimüslim haklarının korunması ve lüks yaşamdan kaçınması ile tanınır. Halifeliği yalnızca iki buçuk yıl sürmüş olmasına rağmen, İslam siyaset düşüncesinde ideal yönetici modeli olarak referans gösterilir.
ei1:omar-n-abd-al-aziz.narrative_en: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz was the eighth Umayyad caliph, remembered as the 'fifth rightly-guided caliph' for his justice and reform policies. His order for the official compilation of hadiths marks a turning point in Islamic intellectual history. He was known for tax justice, protection of non-Muslim rights, and avoidance of luxury. Despite his caliphate lasting only two and a half years, he is referenced as the ideal ruler model in Islamic political thought.
ei1:omar-n-abd-al-aziz.narrative_ar: عمر بن عبد العزيز الخليفة الاموي الثامن المعروف بعدله وسياسات الاصلاح حتى لقب بالخليفة الراشد الخامس. كان اول خليفة امر بالجمع الرسمي للحديث مما يجعله نقطة تحول في تاريخ العلوم الاسلامية. اشتهر بعدالة الضرائب وحماية حقوق غير المسلمين واجتناب الترف. رغم ان خلافته لم تدم سوى سنتين ونصف الا انه يضرب به المثل كنموذج الحاكم المثالي في الفكر السياسي الاسلاميترك عمر بن عبد العزيز إرثاً فقهياً وإدارياً مؤثراً، حيث وضع أسساً للحكم الرشيد تُدرّس في كتب الفقه السياسي حتى اليوم. يُعتبر مثالاً نادراً للحاكم الذي جمع بين السلطة السياسية والتقوى الشخصية، مما جعل فترة حكمه القصيرة نموذجاً يُحتذى به عبر التاريخ الإسلامي.

ei1:omar-khaivam.narrative_en: Omar Khayyam was both a profound mathematician-astronomer and one of world literature's most famous poets. He systematized geometric solutions to cubic equations; his Jalali calendar is more accurate than the Gregorian. His Rubaiyat gained worldwide fame through Fitz Gerald's translation. His poems exploring wine, transience, and philosophical skepticism made him one of the most universal voices inmedieval Persian literature, bridging the mystical traditions of Sufism with rational inquiry into the nature of existence and divine providence. His philosophical verse challenged orthodox religious certainties while maintaining profound spiritual depth, establishing him as both a rigorous mathematician-astronomer and one of Islam's greatest contemplative poets.

ei1:rabia-al-adawiya.narrative_en: Rabia al-Adawiyya is the most important female mystic in the history of Islamic Sufism. Born into a poor family in Basra and having experienced slavery, she devoted herself entirely to worship and spiritual life. She is credited as the first to place divine love at the center of Sufi thought. Her famous saying—asking God not to let her worship out of fear of hell or desire for paradise but solely for His sake—is one of the best-known expressions in Sufi literature.

ei1:shibli-numani.narrative_en: Shibli Numani was one of the most important Islamic historians of the Indian subcontinent and author of Sirat al-Nabi, a comprehensive prophetic biography. His work is considered one of the most valuable biographies written with modern historical methodology. He taught at Aligarh and Nadwat al-Ulama. His monographs on al-Mamun, al-Faruq, and al-Ghazali are also important studies. He passed away before completing his work, which was finished by his student Sulayman Nadwi.

ei1:wasil-b.narrative_en: Wasil ibn Ata is recognized as the founder of the Mutazila school in Islamic theological history. His departure from the study circle of Hasan al-Basri over the question of the status of the grave sinner gave rise to the concept of 'itizal' (withdrawal). He formulated the principle of al-manzila bayn al-manzilatayn (a position between two positions). As a pioneer of rationalist theological methodology, he laid the foundation of the rationalist tradition in Islamic thought. He was also known for his powerful oratory.
